prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

An apparatus for axially adjusting a shifting element includes a shifting shaft, which can be rotated about an axis, an actuating body, which is connected to the shifting shaft for conjoint rotation and in an axially movable manner and which has at least two slotted guide sections designed as grooves on a peripheral surface, and a linear actuator, which is associated with the actuating body and has an actuatable actuator pin, which can engage in the slotted guide sections in order to axially move the actuating body. Each slotted guide section has an incoupling region for the actuator pin, an opposite outcoupling region for the actuator pin, and an adjusting region, which lies therebetween in the peripheral direction and is bent in a curved shape, for axially moving the actuating body. The incoupling region and the outcoupling region of the slotted guide sections that are adjacent in the peripheral direction are arranged at the same axial position.

outputs.L1: An apparatus for axially adjusting a shifting element comprises a shifting shaft rotatable about an axis; an actuating body connected to the shifting shaft for conjoint rotation and axial movement, the actuating body having at least two slotted guide sections formed as grooves in a peripheral surface; and a linear actuator associated with the actuating body and having an actuatable actuator pin configured to engage the slotted guide sections to axially move the actuating body. Each slotted guide section includes an incoupling region for the actuator pin, an opposite outcoupling region for the actuator pin, and a curved adjusting region located therebetween in the peripheral direction for axially moving the actuating body. The incoupling region and the outcoupling region of slotted guide sections adjacent in the peripheral direction are arranged at the same axial position.
outputs.L2: A device for changing the axial position of a shifting element comprises a shifting shaft rotatable about an axis and an actuating body coupled to the shaft so that they rotate together while the body remains axially displaceable. At least two groove-shaped guide tracks are formed on the actuating body’s circumferential surface. A linear actuator assigned to the actuating body includes an operable actuator pin that can enter these guide tracks to shift the actuating body axially. Each guide track comprises an entry region for receiving the pin, an opposing exit region, and a curved adjustment region extending circumferentially between the entry and exit regions to produce axial movement of the actuating body. For guide tracks next to one another in the circumferential direction, the entry region of one track and the exit region of the adjacent track are located at an identical axial position.
outputs.L3:
The apparatus is configured to axially adjust a shifting element by means of a shifting shaft that is rotatable about an axis. An actuating body is connected to the shifting shaft in a rotationally conjoint manner, while remaining movable in the axial direction relative to the shaft.

At least two slotted guide sections are formed as grooves in the peripheral surface of the actuating body. A linear actuator includes an actuator pin that engages these guide sections. Linear movement of the actuator pin within the grooves causes the actuating body, and thus the shifting element, to move axially.

Each slotted guide section comprises an incoupling region, a curved adjusting region, and an outcoupling region. The incoupling region guides the actuator pin into the respective guide section, the curved adjusting region converts the interaction between the actuator pin and the rotating actuating body into axial displacement, and the outcoupling region allows the actuator pin to disengage. The guide sections are arranged so that the incoupling region of one section and the outcoupling region of an adjacent section are located at the same axial position, thereby facilitating smooth and reliable transitions between the guide sections.
outputs.L4:
An apparatus for axially adjusting a shifting element includes a rotatable shifting shaft, an actuating body arranged on the shifting shaft so as to be axially movable, and a linear actuator having an actuator pin. The actuating body is provided with a plurality of curved slotted-guide grooves distributed around its circumference. The actuator pin engages one of the grooves and, during rotation of the shifting shaft, follows the curved path of that groove. Because the actuator pin is constrained to move linearly, its engagement with the curved groove converts the rotational movement of the shifting shaft into an axial displacement of the actuating body and, consequently, of the shifting element coupled to the actuating body.

Each slotted-guide groove has an incoupling region, a guide region, and an outcoupling region. The outcoupling region of one groove and the incoupling region of an adjacent groove are positioned at substantially the same axial location on the actuating body. As a result, the actuator pin can leave one groove and enter the next without requiring a compensating axial movement or producing an abrupt change in the position of the actuating body. Successive grooves can therefore be engaged in sequence to provide controlled, repeatable axial adjustment over multiple shifting positions. This arrangement reduces discontinuities, impact loads, and the risk of jamming during groove transitions, thereby enabling smooth shifting and reliable operation of the apparatus.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract describing an apparatus for axially adjusting a shifting element using a rotatable shifting shaft, a grooved actuating body, and a linear actuator pin.
counterfactuals.output: An apparatus for axially adjusting a shifting element includes a shifting shaft rotatable about a longitudinal axis, an actuating body coupled to the shifting shaft for rotation therewith, and an actuator pin operatively connected to the shifting element. The actuating body includes a guide groove extending with an axial component about the longitudinal axis. The actuator pin engages the guide groove and is constrained against rotation while being movable in an axial direction. Rotation of the shifting shaft causes the guide groove to displace the actuator pin axially, thereby moving the shifting element between at least first and second operating positions. The geometry of the guide groove may define the displacement path, transmission ratio, and one or more holding positions of the shifting element.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the key features of a transmission shift-adjustment mechanism in which an actuator pin engages curved slotted guide sections to produce axial movement.
counterfactuals.output:
- **Rotary-to-axial motion conversion:** Movement of an actuator causes a pin to travel through one or more curved guide slots, forcing the associated shift member to move axially.  
- **Defined shift path:** The curvature and pitch of the slotted guide sections determine the direction, travel, and rate of axial displacement.  
- **Multiple guide sections:** Successive or oppositely curved slot portions can provide different shift phases, reverse the axial direction, or create dwell/neutral regions.  
- **Positive mechanical guidance:** The pin-and-slot engagement constrains the shift member along a repeatable path, improving gear-position accuracy.  
- **Compact construction:** The mechanism combines guidance and actuation without requiring a separate linear actuator or complex linkage.  
- **Controlled shift behavior:** Slot geometry can be tailored to vary mechanical advantage, reduce shift effort, and smooth engagement between transmission positions.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe a mechanical device that converts rotational motion of a shifting shaft into controlled axial displacement through multiple curved guide grooves and an engageable actuator pin.
counterfactuals.output:
A **multi-groove barrel-cam mechanism** can perform this conversion. A cylindrical cam is fixed to or rotates with the shifting shaft and carries several curved guide grooves around its circumference. An actuator pin, connected to an axially movable member such as a shift fork or sleeve, can be selectively engaged with one of the grooves.

As the shaft rotates, the selected groove’s helical or curved path forces the pin to travel parallel to the shaft axis, producing a predetermined axial displacement. Different grooves can provide different stroke lengths, directions, timing, or dwell periods. Disengaging and re-engaging the pin with another groove allows the same shaft rotation to generate a different controlled axial movement.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a concise technical disclosure for a gear-shifting actuator whose adjacent slotted guides have their outcoupling and incoupling regions at the same axial position.
counterfactuals.output:
### Gear-Shifting Actuator with Axially Aligned Guide Transitions

A gear-shifting actuator includes a movable selector element and at least two adjacent slotted guides arranged along an actuator axis. Each slotted guide receives a follower coupled to a gear-selection member and includes a control region, an outcoupling region, and an incoupling region. The outcoupling region of a first slotted guide and the incoupling region of an adjacent second slotted guide are located at substantially the same axial position.

During actuator movement, the follower can therefore disengage from the first slotted guide and engage the second slotted guide without an intervening axial displacement. The aligned transition reduces actuator travel, permits a compact guide arrangement, and limits unintended movement of the gear-selection member during transfer. Transition surfaces may be ramped, curved, or chamfered to provide continuous follower guidance and reduce impact, wear, and shifting noise.

The actuator may be implemented as a rotatable shift drum, an axially translating guide body, or a combined rotary-linear actuator. The slotted guides may be formed integrally in the actuator body or provided as separate guide inserts.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
